chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the least thing that makes a person a mushrik (polytheist). He said: 'The one who initiates an opinion, then loves it or hates over it.'

key_terms.أَبْغَضَ عَلَيْهِ: Hated it (the truth/other views) over (the opinion)
key_terms.أَحَبَّ عَلَيْهِ: Loved it (the opinion) over (the truth/other views)
key_terms.مُشْرِكاً: Polytheist; one who associates partners with God

ai.seo_question: What is the smallest form of shirk according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) redefines the minimal threshold of shirk as an internal psychological rigidity where one loves their own subjective opinion (ra'y) above truth or hates it when it contradicts their bias. This shifts the focus from external idol worship to the internal attachment to self-constructed dogma, a concept central to Shia epistemology. It highlights how subjective preference can become a form of associating partners with God by elevating personal judgment to the status of divine truth.
